subject: SCIENCE
prompt: What is the basic unit of structure and function in all living things?
choices: Atom
Cell
Tissue
Organ
explanation: All living things are made of one or more cells. The cell is the smallest unit that can be said to be alive.

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: Which of the following best describes the role of the cell membrane?
choices: It stores genetic information
It converts sunlight into food
It releases energy from food molecules
It controls what enters and leaves the cell
correctAnswer: It controls what enters and leaves the cell
explanation: The cell membrane is a selectively permeable boundary that regulates which substances move into and out of the cell.

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: In the water cycle, the process in which liquid water changes into water vapor is called ___.
explanation: Energy from the Sun causes liquid water to evaporate, changing into water vapor (a gas) that enters the atmosphere.

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: In which direction does thermal energy move on its own?
choices: From warmer objects to cooler objects
From cooler objects to warmer objects
From larger objects to smaller objects
From heavier objects to lighter objects
correctAnswer: From warmer objects to cooler objects
explanation: Thermal energy is transferred spontaneously from hotter regions or objects to colder ones until they reach the same temperature.

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: Which gas released by burning fossil fuels is a major greenhouse gas?
choices: Oxygen
Nitrogen
Carbon dioxide
Helium
explanation: Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide, a greenhouse gas that traps heat in Earth's atmosphere.

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: Order the levels of organization in a multicellular organism from smallest to largest.
explanation: Cells form tissues, tissues form organs, organs work together in organ systems, and organ systems make up the organism.

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: Which organelle releases energy from food molecules for the cell to use?
choices: Nucleus
Chloroplast
Mitochondrion
Cell wall
explanation: Mitochondria carry out cellular respiration, releasing energy from food molecules. Chloroplasts capture light energy to make food; the nucleus holds genetic material.

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: Which statement is supported by the passage?
passage: Scientists analyzed records of average global temperature going back to the 1800s. The data showed that the average global temperature increased by approximately 1.1 degrees Celsius between 1880 and 2020. The rate of warming has accelerated since the 1970s, with each of the last four decades being warmer than any decade that preceded it since 1850. Researchers attribute much of this warming to the increased concentration of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere, primarily from burning fossil fuels.
choices: Global temperature has risen at the same steady rate since 1880
The rate of warming has increased since the 1970s
Average global temperature decreased between 1880 and 2020
Most of the warming is attributed to volcanic eruptions
correctAnswer: The rate of warming has increased since the 1970s
explanation: The passage states that the rate of warming has accelerated since the 1970s and that researchers attribute much of the warming to greenhouse gases from burning fossil fuels.

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: A strawberry plant sends out a runner that grows into a new plant (asexual reproduction). How does the new plant's genetic information compare with the parent's?
choices: It is identical to the parent's
It is a mix from two different parents
It is completely different from the parent's
It has half as many genes as the parent
correctAnswer: It is identical to the parent's
explanation: Asexual reproduction involves one parent and produces offspring with genetic information identical to the parent's. Sexual reproduction combines genetic information from two parents, producing variation.

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: Which of these materials are good thermal insulators (they slow the transfer of thermal energy)? Select all that apply.
choices: Plastic foam
Copper
Wool
Aluminum
Air trapped in feathers
explanation: Foam, wool, and trapped air transfer thermal energy slowly, so they are good insulators. Metals such as copper and aluminum are good conductors.

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: Why are places near the equator generally warmer than places near the poles?
choices: The equator is much closer to the Sun
The equator has more volcanoes
The air is thinner at the equator
The equator receives more direct sunlight
correctAnswer: The equator receives more direct sunlight
explanation: Because Earth is a sphere, sunlight strikes the equator more directly and is more concentrated there. Near the poles the same sunlight is spread over a larger area.

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: Word bank: condensation, precipitation, evaporation. Fill in the blanks. When water vapor cools and changes into liquid droplets that form clouds, the process is called ___. Water that falls from clouds as rain, snow, or hail is called ___.
explanation: Condensation is the change from water vapor to liquid water. Precipitation is water falling from clouds to Earth's surface.

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: You touch a hot pan and quickly pull your hand away. Which path does the information follow?
choices: Muscles in the hand, then nerves, then the brain, then receptors in the skin
Receptors in the skin, then nerves, then spinal cord and brain, then muscles
The brain first, then blood vessels, then the heart, then receptors in the skin
Receptors in the skin, then blood, then the heart, then muscles of the hand
correctAnswer: Receptors in the skin, then nerves, then spinal cord and brain, then muscles
explanation: Sensory receptors in the skin detect the heat and send signals along nerves to the spinal cord and brain, and signals then travel to the muscles that move the hand. In a fast reflex like this, the spinal cord sends the signal to the muscles even before the brain notices the pain.

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: Which conclusion is best supported by the data?
passage: A student heated two beakers of water on identical hot plates for 5 minutes. Both began at 20 degrees C. Beaker A held 100 g of water and ended at 60 degrees C. Beaker B held 200 g of water and ended at 40 degrees C.
choices: Beaker B received less energy than Beaker A, because it ended at a lower temperature
The water in Beaker B is a different substance
With the same energy added, a larger mass of water has a smaller temperature change
Temperature change does not depend on the mass of the water
correctAnswer: With the same energy added, a larger mass of water has a smaller temperature change
explanation: Both beakers received the same energy from identical hot plates for the same time. Beaker B had twice the mass and half the temperature change (20 degrees C compared with 40 degrees C), so temperature change depends on the mass of the sample.

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: A student tests which cup keeps hot water warm the longest. She pours the same amount of water at the same starting temperature into a foam cup, a paper cup, and a metal cup, then measures each temperature after 10 minutes. What is the independent variable?
choices: The temperature after 10 minutes
The material of the cup
The amount of water
The starting temperature of the water
explanation: The independent variable is the one the experimenter changes on purpose: the cup material. The temperature after 10 minutes is the dependent variable, and the amount of water and starting temperature are controlled variables.

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: A cold air mass moves into a region of warm, humid air. What weather is most likely along the boundary between them?
choices: Clear skies, because the cold air holds more water vapor than the warm air does
No change in the weather, because air masses never interact with each other
Dry, calm weather, because the warm, humid air sinks below the cold air mass
Clouds and precipitation, as the warm, humid air is pushed up and cools
correctAnswer: Clouds and precipitation, as the warm, humid air is pushed up and cools
explanation: At a cold front, denser cold air pushes under the warm, humid air. The warm air rises and cools, its water vapor condenses, and clouds and precipitation (often storms) form.

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: During exercise, both your breathing rate and your heart rate increase. What is the best explanation?
choices: The respiratory and circulatory systems work together to get more oxygen to muscle cells
The two systems work independently, and the increases just happen at the same time by chance
The digestive system needs more air during exercise, so the lungs and heart speed up
The heart makes extra oxygen during exercise, and the lungs carry it out to the muscles
correctAnswer: The respiratory and circulatory systems work together to get more oxygen to muscle cells
explanation: Body systems interact. Working muscle cells need more oxygen, so the lungs take in oxygen faster and the heart pumps blood faster to deliver it and remove carbon dioxide.

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: Two cuttings from the same plant are genetically identical. One is grown in full sun with fertilizer, and the other in shade with poor soil. After two months the first plant is much taller. What does this show?
choices: The taller plant's genes changed as it grew because it got more sunlight
The growth of a plant depends only on its genes
Environmental factors, as well as genes, affect how an organism grows
The two plants must have had different parents
correctAnswer: Environmental factors, as well as genes, affect how an organism grows
explanation: The plants have the same genes, so the difference in growth must be due to environmental factors such as light and nutrients. Both genetic and environmental factors influence growth.
